stops.note: Louis Braille, blinded at three in his father's harness workshop at Coupvray, devised his six-dot code at 15 in 1824, adapting Charles Barbier's army 'night writing'
Britain's British and Foreign Blind Association, founded by Thomas Rhodes Armitage in 1868, campaigned for braille over rival raised-letter systems

current_meaning: a writing system of raised dots read by touch
